target = ".......((((.((((.(((.(((....))).(((.(((....))).(((.(((....))).(((.(((....))).(((......))).))).))).))).))).(....).)))).((((...(((.(((...((....))........))).(((.(((....)))(((....)))(((....)))))).)))...((((.(....).(((.(((.(((.(((.(((...(((....))).))).(((....))).))).(((....))).))).(((....))).))).((((((....)))(((....))).(((....)))))).))).))))...)))).))))......."
assert len(target) == 358, len(target)

# parse pairs
stack = []
pairs = {}
for i,c in enumerate(target):
    if c == '(':
        stack.append(i)
    elif c == ')':
        j = stack.pop()
        pairs[j] = i
        pairs[i] = j

import random
random.seed(42)

# Assign pairs: rotate through GC, CG, AU, UA to keep variety but stable
pair_bases = ["GC","CG","AU","UA","GU","UG"]
seq = list('A'*358)
# order pairs by outermost
pairlist = sorted(set(tuple(sorted(p)) for p in pairs.items()))
for idx,(i,j) in enumerate(pairlist):
    b = pair_bases[idx % len(pair_bases)]
    seq[i] = b[0]
    seq[j] = b[1]

# loops: hairpin loops use GAAA or UUCG-ish; loops get A-rich
# unpaired positions: assign A mostly, with some U
for i,c in enumerate(target):
    if c == '.':
        seq[i] = 'A'
# Add some variety in loops to avoid issues - put U in middle of longer loops
print(''.join(seq))
EOF
